claims.claim: The Cardiff Giant was about ten feet of stone presented as a petrified/fossil man
claims.quote: It was a 10-foot-tall (3.0 m), roughly 3,000 pound purported "petrified man", uncovered on October 16, 1869

claims.claim: It was exhumed at Cardiff, Onondaga County, New York, on 16 October 1869
claims.quote: EXHUMED AT CARDIFF, ONONDAGA CO., N. Y., OCT. 16, 1869.

claims.claim: The lithograph is titled "The Onondaga Giant" and is credited to Popular Graphic Arts
claims.quote: THE ONONDAGA GIANT.

claims.claim: Andrew D. White was of Cornell and inspected the giant/site closely
claims.quote: Andrew D. White, the first president of Cornell University, made a close inspection of the Cardiff Giant.

claims.claim: The spot was convenient to neither the house nor the barn, and a good spring and stream of water already ran to both
claims.quote: that it was convenient neither to the house nor to the barn; that there was already a good spring and a stream of water running conveniently to both

claims.claim: White called the whole matter a hoax
claims.quote: my answer was that the whole matter was undoubtedly a hoax

claims.claim: The photograph of the giant is a Bain News Service image dated 1910
claims.quote:
Date: 1910
Author: Bain News Service, publisher

claims.claim: In 1868 George Hull and H. B. Martin hired men to quarry a gypsum block ten feet four and a half inches long at Fort Dodge, Iowa
claims.quote: In 1868, Hull, accompanied by a man named H. B. Martin, hired men to quarry out a 10-foot-4.5-inch-long (3.2 m) block of gypsum in Fort Dodge, Iowa

claims.claim: The quarrymen were told the block was intended for a monument to Abraham Lincoln in New York
claims.quote: telling them it was intended for a monument to Abraham Lincoln in New York

claims.claim: The stereocard shows Cardiff Glen, near Fort Dodge, Iowa, and dates from 1873
claims.quote:
View in Cardiff Glen, near Fort Dodge, Iowa.
Date: 1873

claims.claim: The printed caption on the back of the stereocard names George Hull and H. B. Martin as the perpetrators
claims.quote: The perpetrators of the imposture are well remembered by old residents of Fort Dodge. Their names were George Hull and H. B. Martin.

claims.claim: The card back describes the route: block taken from the gypsum quarry to Chicago, the giant carved, then shipped to New York, buried in a barn lot and subsequently "discovered"
claims.quote: The block was taken to Chicago, the "Giant" carved, and then shipped to the point in New York which gave it its name, where it was buried in a barn lot, and subsequently "discovered".

claims.claim: The lithograph sheet lists the nose as six inches
claims.quote: length of nose, 6 inches

claims.claim: The sheet lists whole length 10 feet 4½ inches, mouth 4 inches, palm 7 inches
claims.quote: Whole length of the figure, 10 feet, 4½ inches; ... width of mouth, 4 inches; ... width of palm, 7 inches

claims.claim: Yale's O. C. Marsh found fresh tool marks on soluble gypsum and called it "a most decided humbug"
claims.quote: Yale paleontologist Othniel C. Marsh examined the statue, pointing out that it was made of soluble gypsum, which, had it been buried in its blanket of wet earth for centuries, would not still have fresh tool marks on it (which it did), and termed it "a most decided humbug".

claims.claim: Henry Salle and Fred Mohrmann carved the giant for Chicago stonecutter Edward Burkhardt
claims.quote: He shipped the block to Edward Burkhardt in Chicago, a German stonecutter. Burkhardt hired two sculptors named Henry Salle and Fred Mohrmann to create the giant.

claims.claim: Quilts were hung to lessen the sound of the carving
claims.quote: it is reported that they took steps to cover up their work during the carving, putting up quilts to lessen the sound of carving

claims.claim: It is not clear whether Burkhardt knew what Hull intended
claims.quote: While it is not clear if Burkhardt was aware of Hull's intentions

claims.claim: Hull confessed on 10 December 1869
claims.quote: On December 10, 1869, Hull confessed everything to the press

claims.claim: Both giants were declared fakes in court on 2 February 1870
claims.quote: on February 2, 1870, both giants were revealed as fakes in court

claims.claim: George Hull was a New York tobacconist
claims.quote: The giant was the creation of a New York tobacconist named George Hull.

claims.claim: The figure was modelled on Hull himself
claims.quote: The giant was designed to imitate the form of Hull himself.

claims.claim: Sand, sulphuric acid and steel knitting needles were used to age the surface and give it pores
claims.quote: Hull first wiped the giant using a sponge soaked with sand and water. The giant's surface was beaten with steel knitting needles embedded in a board to simulate pores. The giant was also rubbed with sulphuric acid to create a deeper, vintage-like color.

claims.claim: A geologist told Hull hair would not petrify, so the figure was made hairless
claims.quote: Hull consulted a geologist and learned that hairs would not be petrified, so he removed the hair and beard from the giant.

claims.claim: It was buried on his cousin William Newell's farm in Cardiff, New York, in late November 1868
claims.quote: On a night in late November 1868, the giant was buried in a hole in Newell's farm.

claims.claim: Hired well-diggers found it on 16 October 1869
claims.quote: Newell hired Gideon Emmons and Henry Nichols, ostensibly to dig a well, and on October 16, 1869, they found the giant

claims.claim: Newell charged fifty cents for a fifteen-minute viewing
claims.quote: Newell charged each visitor fifty cents for a fifteen-minute session of viewing the giant

claims.claim: Three to five hundred people came per day
claims.quote: The number of visitors went to about three to five hundred per day

claims.claim: Hull said he confessed to show how easily people believe
claims.quote: confessed proudly that he intended for the hoax to be exposed to reveal the tendency of the Christian community to believe in things too easily

claims.claim: P. T. Barnum had the giant copied covertly in wax
claims.quote: he hired a man to model the giant's shape covertly in wax and create a plaster copy

claims.claim: That Barnum's copy is the one in a Michigan arcade museum is only a claim made by its owner
claims.quote: The owner of Marvin's Marvelous Mechanical Museum, a coin-operated game arcade and museum of oddities in Farmington Hills, Michigan, has said that the copy displayed there is Barnum's.

claims.claim: The images include both sides of the 1873 stereocard (front view and printed verso)
claims.quote: VIEW IN CARDIFF GLEN. NEAR FORT DODGE.IOWA.
